correctness.rationale: Ultrahomogeneity reduces complete finite-base \(1\)-types to one-point extension types. Every finite base has a nondecreasing Ferrers threshold sequence. Inserting a new second-order column leaves one free initial-segment choice inside the threshold block; irreflexivity forces the new row threshold strictly past its own column. Counting compatible first-order row cuts and summing over all column cuts gives \((m+1)(2m+1)\) distinct-point types, and adding the \(m\) equality types gives \(2(m+1)^2-1\). Exhaustive finite replay independently enumerates every valid base through \(m=5\) and all threshold shapes through \(m=8\).
